correctness.rationale: The dual vertex classification follows from connected tight-edge graphs. The strict two-move screening lemma has positive explicit gaps for each of \(y=0\), \(s>t\), and \(t\ge s\), eliminating every maximizing \(x>0\). The remaining quadratic is strictly concave in the integer y, and full contact-normal ranks give the affine dimensions. Exact independent signed spanning-tree enumeration reconstructs all polar vertices and contact ranks in seven cases; a larger rational grid tests the screening inequality. The analytical proof covers arbitrary real radii; finite checks are supplementary.

value.rationale: The exact canonical Euclidean inradius and set of all incenters are natural geometric invariants of a family of ultrametric transportation spaces. A strict majority-minority screening principle unexpectedly removes dependence on the minority internal length, while a natural rational imbalance threshold changes incenter-locus dimension by \(q-1\) and triggers a binomial sequence of contact facets. Unlike a facet recount or isolated table value, the result is an infinite, all-real-parameter structural classification of geometric phase changes.
